title: Mole’s Child
text: “Wolf, just because Theo’s turned into a rabbit doesn’t mean you can attack her because your instincts got triggered, okay?”
“Woof, Wolf knows. Besides, Theo was raised by Spear Hero, so she’s tough—her fur’s hard as rock.”
“She did nip at me playfully once before. Bit down pretty hard too, but sure enough it didn’t hurt at all, so that was a relief.”
That was thanks to making her sturdy enough to withstand a kick from Filo-tan, I say.
“Sure would be nice if someone other than me and the old man could help drum up customers…”
muttered Panda, sprawled out lazily, watching the bustling crowd.
This was after that evening’s performance. Father had gone out to purchase slaves… and mixed in among the slaves he’d bought was a mole!
“Father! It’s a mole, I say!”
I pointed at the trembling mole in the cage and said so to Father.
“Ah… yeah…”
Father, who’d been tending to her, nodded while casting a sympathetic look at the trembling mole. She bore some painful-looking whip marks.
“Uu…”

The mole was huddled under a blanket, shivering. It seemed Father had also sensed that this mole was just a child. He looked troubled, wondering whether to leave her to the accompanying Siltvelt envoy or the monster dealer’s subordinates. Once Father stepped out of the cage area to a spot where the mole couldn’t hear us, I made my proposal once more.
“Father, you must take that mole under your protection. And you should take great care of her, I say.”
“Is there something special about her?”
“She’s a mole that Father protects in world after world, starting from the very first world, I say. She’s skilled in all sorts of ways and quite useful, indeed.”

Above all, this was a mole who—much like Big Sister—would apparently grow up only to become a spirit after death. Considering the contents of that dream, I needed to take proper care of her now and bank the goodwill. Worst case, raising her up to become a partner for Father wasn’t a bad option either… though getting her to grow into someone matching Father’s tastes seemed about as difficult as it had been with Big Sister. And yet… I recalled hearing that she’d beaten Big Sister at something once. I couldn’t quite recall what it was she’d won at, though. According to the mole’s own testimony, it seemed to be because she resembled young Big Sister. But I had a feeling there was something more to it than that. Every time I got close to remembering after meeting the mole-turned-spirit, the memory slipped away. In my memories, Big Sister would say, with a chillingly composed face, “You don’t need to remember that.” Incidentally, the mole was the one person, aside from Assistant, whom Rival called “sister.”
“I see… so she’s a kid I’m allowed to take in. That’s a relief.”
Father looked visibly relieved as he gazed at the cage holding the mole. I wondered what that was about. When I tilted my head, Father gave a wry smile.
“Ah, well… being involved in all this buying and selling as a slave trader, I end up wanting to take care of every single kid, you know? None of them chose to become slaves, after all…”
Father was so kind-hearted that he was deeply troubled by his work as a slave trader. Yet he held himself back, knowing he couldn’t save every single slave out there.
“But that girl really did stand out to me more than the others, somehow… I haven’t heard her name yet, but I’ll take her in.”
“Splendid, I say. Only… you’ll need to be careful about how she interacts with Filolial-sama.”

Kou wasn’t the only one who kept stepping on landmines and getting punished for it—there were other Filolial-samas too, who’d occasionally declare the mole looked delicious and end up getting scolded or punished for it. I resolved to ask Elephant and the others to educate everyone on that front. And for any Filolial-sama who still wouldn’t listen even after that… well, uu, I say. In any case, the mole could no longer be treated carelessly. Here, the wisest course was to build up a tremendous debt of gratitude. Yes, I needed to keep thinking of ways to deepen the bond between her and Father as much as possible going forward. But then a thought occurred to me. This mole… when the time came to help Father, how exactly was I supposed to arrange the encounter? I already knew the location of the mole’s burrow from the loop where we’d all headed to Faubrey together, but when the Melromarc incident was resolved by bringing back the Queen and the others, they’d be cracking down on slave hunters, meaning the mole wouldn’t end up a victim after all. If that were the case, her parents would still be alive and she’d be living in the burrow. So how was I supposed to recruit her from there? Even supposing I helped Father, could I really guide him all the way to the mole’s burrow… and bring her back? I doubted it. That left one option: buy her the very first time she was put up for sale as a slave, transport her, and arrange for her to be placed with Father while he was still reeling from the false charges against him. At this point, in my memories, Big Sister’s expression grew complicated.
‘I think it’s fine to save her if you can save her. After all, her parents are still alive at the point in time you’d be returning to.’

is what she seemed to be saying. Hmm… I say. Still, getting her and Father to bond well was a solid strategy. The question was how best to bring the mole into the fold while her parents were still alive. Come to think of it, I recalled hearing somewhere that Heroes occupy the “prince” role in fairy tales and the like. Wasn’t that something Father mentioned recently when he heard the fairy tale that Rabbit Guy knew? If that were the case, then perhaps even a sudden, out-of-nowhere recruitment attempt on the mole would have her parents handing her over without much fuss. I myself had experience raising up a plain, self-deprecating girl before. She’d grown into a pig confident enough to speak her mind, captivating all the men around her. Her rank as a pig had likely gone up because of it. Well, I could think about all that once the time actually came. Since she reportedly had a spirit very similar to Big Sister’s, depending on circumstances, I might consider having her serve as a stand-in for Big Sister. Timing-wise, whether she’d even count as a slave was extremely questionable. That said, deliberately tipping off slave hunters about the mole’s burrow just to speed up her fall into slavery was absolutely out of the question. Pull a stunt like that, and I’d undoubtedly get reported straight to Big Sister.
“Motoyasu-kun?”
“What is it, I say?”
“No, it’s just—you looked so deep in thought, I figured maybe you were worried the Filolials might target her.”
“Indeed, I say… I’ll be asking Elephant and Big Sister and the others to handle that, so until then, please make sure she stays close by your side and doesn’t wander off.”
“Yeah. Got it. Everyone else is kind too, so let’s take good care of her.”
And so it was that Father took to caring for the mole.

This was some time after Rabbit Guy had fully transformed into a giant rabbit and taken the mole under his protection. Rafumi, who’d been serving as Ren’s body double, happened to be near the town where we were putting on our circus performance, and came running into the circus grounds—where Ren’s companions were training alongside Kuro-chan—to call out to Father and Ren.
“Haah… haah… Ren-sama, Shield Hero-sama! Please, come with us!”
If I recalled correctly, they were two of Ren’s companions—one who seemed to be the second-string mage, not the leader, and the other looking like a sullen, taciturn woodcutter type.
“…What happened?”
Ren replied to his companions with a look that practically screamed “after everything, you’ve got the nerve to show your face here,” his tone carrying a distinct emotional distance.
